question: A 50 years old man was recently diagnosed to be having coronary artery disease. There was no added risk factors except for a LDL value of 150-165mgs/dl. The single drug most appropriate for initial therapy is
analysis: In a patient with coronary artery disease and elevated LDL cholesterol levels, statins are the first-line treatment. Statins are well-established for their efficacy in lowering LDL cholesterol and reducing cardiovascular risk. The other options, such as gemfibrozil, nicotinic acid, and bile acid binding resins, are not typically used as first-line treatments for isolated elevated LDL levels in the context of coronary artery disease.
